takeaway: Silhouette makes persistent-memory file-system crash testing tractable by recognizing stores protected by known consistency mechanisms and applying a two-plan heuristic only to the remaining stores.
background: Persistent-memory writes can remain in volatile CPU caches and can be reordered, so file systems use flushes, fences, journaling, log-structured writes, and replication to guarantee recoverable states. Crash testers construct possible persisted images and run recovery checks.
villain: Exhaustively choosing which in-flight stores survive a crash creates an exponential image space. Prior file-system tools prune it by recovery reads or cache-line flushes, but still generate large numbers of plans and can miss bugs outside their validation scope.
approach: Silhouette combines LLVM instrumentation, runtime data-type tracking, and lightweight file-system annotations to identify journaling, log-structured-write, and checksum-replication phases. It checks their ordering invariants, marks their stores protected, hashes duplicate operation traces, and explores two complementary crash plans per unprotected store.
impact: The work shows how domain-specific consistency semantics can replace blind state enumeration. Its invariant-plus-heuristic design expands the tested operations and validation checks while producing orders of magnitude fewer crash plans than prior PM file-system testers.

evaluation.overview: Experiments test PMFS, NOVA-fortis, and WineFS with ACE sequences, custom cases, and NOVA snapshot operations; compare bug-finding time with Vinter and Chipmunk; and measure crash-plan scaling on 50,000 sampled Seq3 cases.
evaluation.implemented: An open-source client-server prototype instruments Linux file-system modules with LLVM, extends Witcher's cache simulator, dynamically maps persistent writes to annotated structure fields, checks mechanism invariants, validates recovered images in QEMU VMs, and deduplicates repeated instruction sequences.
evaluation.setting: Linux 5.1 file-system modules run in Ubuntu 20.04 QEMU VMs on a Dell 7820 with a Xeon Silver 4215R, 144 GB DRAM, and a 2 TB HDD. Each VM has one core, 8 GB DRAM, and a 128 MB DRAM-emulated PM device; scalability tests use ten VMs.

results.text: Silhouette reproduced all 7 bugs reported by Vinter and all 20 reported by Chipmunk, then reported 15 previously unreported bugs across the three file systems; 3 of the new reports had been confirmed and fixed at publication time.

On NOVA with ACE Seq3 over a six-hour window, Silhouette tested 5.3K cases and found 10 bugs in 17 minutes, while Vinter found 4 in 156 minutes after 36 cases and Chipmunk found 6 in 164 minutes after 2.6K cases.
For 50K ACE Seq3 cases, Silhouette generated 14,416, 2,427, and 1,079 crash plans for NOVA, PMFS, and WineFS—reported as 100×–3000× fewer than the original Vinter and Chipmunk runs.

limitations: Silhouette does not systematically explore concurrent thread interleavings. Its two-crash-plan heuristic can miss failures requiring combinations of multiple critical stores, and data mismatches can be false positives requiring manual review. Deploying on another file system requires annotations and, for a new consistency mechanism, new phase and invariant definitions. The study uses three x86 PM file systems, DRAM-emulated PM, and sampled memcpy/memset stores; broader architectures and devices are not evaluated.
phd_group_signal: This is a strong example of systems research that turns file-system semantics into scalable testing machinery: it formalizes persistence phases, bridges source-level types to dynamic traces, builds a recovery harness, and pairs bug case studies with search-space measurements.

claims.text: Silhouette derives update and persistence times from instrumented stores, flushes, and fences, then checks phase-specific ordering invariants for journaling, log-structured writes, and checksum-based replication before classifying their writes as protected.

For each unprotected store, the 2CP strategy tests one image that persists only that store and another that persists every other in-flight store but not it, reducing exploration from combinations of stores to two plans per store.
